candidates.exact_span: Flow shall be estimated daily when discharging.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The phrase "when discharging" makes flow estimation frequency conditional on discharge occurrence; different readings of whether a discharge occurred (or what counts as discharging) change whether daily flow estimation was required and whether missing flow data reflects a no-discharge period, conditional non-requirement, or inadequate evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Estimated flow measurements are not subject to the accuracy provisions established at Part III.C.6 of the permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether Part III.C.6 accuracy provisions apply to estimated flow determines if reported flow can be compared against numeric accuracy or limit provisions; treating estimates as outside those provisions changes which compliance comparisons are applicable.

candidates.exact_span: The pollutant TRC shall be monitored daily when discharging by instantaneous grab which according to Part 136 is defined as analysis within 15 minutes of collection.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Daily TRC monitoring is tied to discharge occurrence, grab sample type, and a 15-minute analysis window; different interpretations of discharging, sample type, or timing requirements change whether monitoring was obligated and how missing or non-instantaneous results are classified.

candidates.exact_span: pH shall continue to be monitored weekly when discharging.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Weekly pH monitoring is conditional on discharging; alternate readings of discharge occurrence or the force of "continue" (carry-forward from a prior permit vs new obligation) change whether weekly pH was required and whether absent pH data reflects conditional non-requirement or missing evidence.

candidates.exact_span: TDS and Cyanide total recoverable shall be monitored once per quarter by grab sample.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Unlike flow, TRC, and pH, this quarterly grab requirement lacks an explicit "when discharging" qualifier; whether quarterly monitoring applies regardless of discharge or is implicitly discharge-conditioned changes which monitoring periods are obligated.

candidates.exact_span: In Section V.C.4.b. above; "Critical Conditions", it was shown that the critical dilution, CD, for the facility is 100%.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Critical dilution (CD) at 100% underpins WET testing design and limit derivation; a different CD value or interpretation of the cited critical-conditions analysis changes which WET limits or testing obligations apply.

candidates.exact_span: for this type of facility the NTIG-WET requires a one-time chronic test.
candidates.computation_change_reason: NTIG-WET classification as requiring a one-time chronic test sets the baseline WET monitoring obligation; whether the facility fits "this type" or whether NTIG-WET mandates chronic (vs acute) testing changes applicable WET monitoring requirements.

candidates.exact_span: Based on the test results, the permit does not require WET limits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether WET limits are absent from the permit determines if WET results are subject to numeric exceedance comparison or are report-only; different readings of what "does not require WET limits" encompasses change applicable limit evaluation for WET parameters.

candidates.exact_span: Therefore, WET limits will not be established in the proposed permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Explicit non-establishment of WET limits means no enforceable numeric WET limit applies; interpreting this as absolute vs contingent on future conditions changes whether WET measurements are compared to numeric limits.

candidates.exact_span: WHOLE EFFLUENT TOXICITY (7day Chronic Static Renewal) (*1)
candidates.computation_change_reason: The specified 7-day chronic static renewal WET test method defines which WET monitoring protocol was required; a different reading of test type or the (*1) cross-reference changes obligated WET monitoring requirements.

Ceriodaphnia dubia WET is report-only (not a numeric limit), once per permit term, and 24-hour composite; interpretations of "Report" vs numeric limit, permit-term timing, and sample type change limit applicability, monitoring obligation windows, and how missing or non-numeric WET results are classified.

Pimephales promelas WET is report-only, once per permit term, and 24-hour composite; different readings of report-only status, permit-term frequency, or composite sample requirements change limit comparisons, monitoring obligations, and missing-evidence semantics for this species' WET results.

candidates.exact_span: *1 Monitoring and reporting requirements begin on the effective date of this permit. See PART II, Whole Effluent Toxicity Testing Requirements for additional WET monitoring and reporting conditions.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Effective-date trigger and the PART II cross-reference define when WET monitoring begins and whether additional conditions apply; different interpretations of start date or incorporated Part II terms change which WET monitoring was required and whether absent data reflects non-applicability or unresolved obligation.

candidates.computation_change_reason: WET testing is limited to once per permit term and tied to first springtime after effective date and irrigation-season return-flow conditions; alternate readings of permit term, springtime window, or irrigation-season discharge likelihood change when WET was required and whether missing WET data reflects conditional non-requirement, documented no-data, or inadequate evidence.
